items.title: Scott Yanow interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, October 22, 2021
items.q: the thing about Charlie Parker let’s say you know like who I’ve always regarded as quite arguably the greatest

ctx.x: Yeah, I like that answer and I asked it partly because you had talked about bop and the fact that sometimes the musicians sacrificed feeling for precision, and emotion for speed.

Well in classic bebop I mean it was such a virtuosic music, you know the music from the mid-40s until 1950 or so that Dizzy Gillespie and Charlie Parker and many others were playing. There is feeling but the notes are often flying by so fast that you know the technique sort of overrides it to an extent. But you know if, the thing about Charlie Parker let’s say you know like who I’ve always regarded as quite arguably the greatest

saxophonist ever, if you slow down his solos to half speed you find that every note makes sense much of the time. It blazes by, you can’t quite follow it if you’re hearing it for the first time or so, but if you listen to it at a slower speed it’s all there, there’s a definite logic.
